production.scenario: GitHub REST API rate limiting enforces a true trailing-minute quota for high-volume OAuth apps at the edge.
components: global integrations driving bursty API traffic from many tenants and regions
service boundary that terminates auth and decides whether requests enter the core API fleet
control-plane service that evaluates the exact trailing minute for each app and route
durable quota ledger in Redis Enterprise with persistence and cross-AZ replication
serves admitted traffic only after quota evaluation completes at the edge
control path that changes tenant limits and emergency suppression rules during incidents
observability path for reject rate, hot tenants, and limiter saturation
flows: Integrations open a burst of authenticated calls that must be evaluated before core service admission.
The gateway sends tenant, route, and timestamp data to the sliding window limiter.
The limiter persists the admitted event in the quota ledger so the next decision uses exact history.
Only requests inside quota cross the service boundary into the REST API fleet.
Abuse and SRE controllers push emergency limits and allowlists into the limiter.
The quota ledger exposes tenant and shard pressure so policy can be tuned before overload.
Dashboards show quota rejects, limiter latency, and policy churn by region and tenant.
